comparison: Both strongly support the track structure observations (C5, C28-C31, C33, C82). OpenEval provides detailed quantitative evidence from Figure 1B showing ~70% of reversals at track ends. Peer reviewers explicitly describe these observations as 'compelling and interesting' and 'potentially ecologically significant.' Full agreement on these fundamental observations.

Both address speed and cell contribution claims (C7-C9, C36-C38, C48, C84). OpenEval finds these SUPPORTED with minor speed discrepancy noted. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 1 challenging the interpretation of Figure 2C as showing 'uniform distribution' and requesting correlation coefficients. The observation is not disputed, but statistical characterization and the inference that all cells contribute are questioned.

Both address dwell time distribution claims (C6, C39-C42, C85). OpenEval finds strong support from quantitative analysis of 1700+ reversal events. Peer review also supports these findings, with Reviewer 1 suggesting the dwell time distribution results should be moved to main text, indicating acceptance of experimental measurements. Full agreement.

Both address agar vs. glass reversal behavior (C43-C46). OpenEval finds support from experimental data showing correlations on agar but not glass. Peer review explicitly supports this, with Reviewer 1 calling the comparison 'interesting' and noting it demonstrates both intrinsic and mechanically triggered reversals. Full agreement.

Both address model structure and capabilities (C50-C55, C86). OpenEval finds the model SUPPORTED, noting it reproduces key observations. Peer review rates UNCERTAIN, acknowledging qualitative success but expressing concerns about limitations. Reviewer 3 states the model is 'a promising hypothesis but not a compelling justification.' Reviewers note the 1D limitation and request more experiments. Divergence on confidence level.

OpenEval R6 addresses model predictions about coupling and synchronization (C10, C56-C62, C87), finding them SUPPORTED but noting mechanistic explanations require validation. Peer R5 addresses broader model evaluation and rates it UNCERTAIN due to qualitative nature and 1D limitations. Partial overlap with different emphasis - OpenEval focuses on parameter exploration, peer review on overall model validation.

Both address cellular coordination during reversals (C11-C12, C64, C88). OpenEval finds strong support from TIRF microscopy tracking. Peer review also strongly supports these observations, with multiple reviewers praising them as 'compelling' and 'concrete experimental evidence.' Full agreement on coordination findings.

Both address rotation-translation coupling (C65-C66, C69, C89). OpenEval finds strong support from angular distribution and speed correlation data (R=0.87). Peer review also strongly supports these observations, with reviewers calling them 'compelling' and 'important clues to the mechanism of motion.' Full agreement on helical motion findings.

Both address slime structure observations (C70-C72). OpenEval finds support from multiple imaging modalities but notes the 'fixed in position' interpretation is somewhat speculative. Peer review supports these findings, with Reviewer 1 stating they 'provide important clues to the mechanism of motion.' Agreement on observations, with OpenEval more cautious about interpretation.

Both address post-reversal acceleration and cell overtaking (C73-C74). OpenEval finds C73 well-supported and C74 more tentative (observed in 'a few filaments'). Peer review supports these as part of the coordination narrative without specific concerns. Agreement, with OpenEval providing more nuanced assessment of evidence strength.

Both address experimental validation of high coupling prediction (C63). OpenEval finds support from Figure 3—figure supplement 4 showing agreement between observed and expected reversals. Peer review also supports this, with Reviewer 1 suggesting it should be in main text. Full agreement on this model validation.

Both address buckling and plectoneme formation in long filaments (C13-C14, C75, C90). OpenEval finds support from 61 observed cases with 400 μm threshold. Peer review also supports these observations, with reviewers noting they have 'potential to shed light on mechanical forces' and 'contains useful information.' Agreement, though reviewers note quantitative analysis is future work.

Both address coordination loss during plectoneme formation (C76-C79, C91). OpenEval finds strong support from detailed tracking analysis showing initial coordination, loss during plectoneme formation, and restoration upon resolution. Peer review also supports these observations as part of the buckling findings. Full agreement on de-coordination during buckling.

Both address plectoneme entanglement and aggregation relevance (C80-C81, C117). OpenEval finds C80 supported by video evidence but notes C81 and C117 are speculative hypotheses. Peer review supports the observation without challenging it, with Reviewer 1 noting buckling observations are relevant to understanding mechanical forces. Agreement on observation, both acknowledge speculative nature of functional interpretation.

Both address biological plausibility of mechano-sensing (C94-C98). OpenEval finds support from genomic evidence and citations but notes direct experimental demonstration is lacking. Peer review supports the plausibility without challenging the genomic evidence, though noting the model requires further validation. Agreement that mechano-sensing is plausible but not directly demonstrated.

OpenEval rates the loss of sensory coupling hypothesis (C92) as UNCERTAIN, noting it is explicitly stated as hypothesis by authors and requires experimental validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found specifically addressing this mechanistic hypothesis.

OpenEval addresses model scope, capabilities, and limitations (C93, C99-C102), finding them SUPPORTED as honest assessments. No specific corresponding peer review result, though peer R5 discusses model limitations more broadly in context of validation concerns.

OpenEval addresses novelty of quantification and rotation-translation coupling mechanism hypothesis (C104-C106), finding them SUPPORTED with appropriate acknowledgment of speculation. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addressing these claims.

OpenEval rates protein complex tracking coinciding with reversals (C111-C113) as UNCERTAIN, noting limited sample size specification and alternative explanations possible. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addressing these observations.

OpenEval finds background and context claims (C1-C4, C15-C27) SUPPORTED by extensive literature citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation as these are established background facts rather than novel findings requiring evaluation.
OpenEval finds the physical constraint about multicellular coordination (C47) SUPPORTED as self-evident. No corresponding peer review evaluation of this basic assumption.
OpenEval finds literature context claims (C107-C110) SUPPORTED by citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation as these provide background context.
OpenEval finds biological context claims (C114-C116, C118) SUPPORTED by prior work citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation of these contextual claims.
OpenEval finds methodological perspective claims (C119-C126) SUPPORTED as reasonable arguments justified by results. No corresponding peer review evaluation of these meta-scientific recommendations.
